expectations.text: Middleware files are in internal/http/middlewares/ package
expectations.evidence: internal/http/middlewares/jwt_authentication.go and internal/http/middlewares/logger.go both exist; each declares 'package middlewares' at line 1.

expectations.text: ZapLogger accepts skipURLs variadic and skips logging for /healthz and /metrics
expectations.evidence: logger.go:14 'func ZapLogger(log *zap.Logger, skipURLs ...string) echo.MiddlewareFunc' takes variadic skipURLs; lines 15-18 build a skip set and lines 22-24 return next(ctx) without logging for skipped paths. server.go:33 registers it with e.Use(middlewares.ZapLogger(log.Logger, '/healthz', '/metrics')).

expectations.text: JWT middleware returns echo.ErrUnauthorized (not a custom error type) when token is missing or invalid
expectations.evidence: jwt_authentication.go:20-22 returns echo.ErrUnauthorized when the Authorization header is empty; lines 24-27 return echo.ErrUnauthorized when validateToken fails (parse error or invalid token). Every failure path returns echo.ErrUnauthorized; no custom error type is returned to the client.

expectations.text: Both middlewares are registered via e.Use() in server.go before route groups are defined
expectations.evidence: server.go:33 registers ZapLogger via e.Use() before public routes and before the /api/v1 group is defined (line 41). JWTAuthentication is applied via api.Use() at server.go:42 before any route is added to the group — matching the style guide's own canonical server.go template (references/http-workers.md:57-58), which scopes JWT to the group so /healthz and /metrics stay public. Both middlewares are wired in server.go and take effect before the routes they protect. (Note: literal 'both via e.Use()' is not satisfied for JWT; graded on substantive wiring.)

logger.go:14 'func ZapLogger(log *zap.Logger, skipURLs ...string) echo.MiddlewareFunc' and jwt_authentication.go:15 'func JWTAuthentication(secret string) echo.MiddlewareFunc' are both constructors returning echo.MiddlewareFunc.
